questions.question_text: The depth of water at a river mouth is modelled by $h(t)=12\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{9}\right)+25$, where $h$ is in metres and $t$ is the number of hours after midnight. What is the depth at $t=3$?

options.why: Used $\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)=1$ instead of $\dfrac{1}{2}$.
Evaluated $\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$ as $-\dfrac{1}{2}$, giving the wrong sign.
Used $\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)=-1$, which is the value at half a period.

questions.question_text: The temperature in a cool room is modelled by $T=-9\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{7}\right)+24$ degrees Celsius. What are the maximum and minimum temperatures the model predicts?

options.why: Swapped the two: the negative coefficient means the maximum occurs when $\cos=-1$.
Read the mean position as the maximum and the coefficient as the minimum.
Added and subtracted twice the amplitude instead of the amplitude itself.

questions.solution_text:
The largest value of $-9\cos$ occurs when $\cos=-1$.
Maximum $=-9\times(-1)+24$
$=33$
Minimum $=-9\times1+24$
$=15$
The maximum is $33^{\circ}$C and the minimum is $15^{\circ}$C.

questions.question_text: The height of the sea surface at a buoy is modelled by $y=40\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{10}\right)+65$ centimetres, where $t$ is in seconds. What is the period of the model?

options.why: Read the $10$ in the denominator as the period, which is only half of it.
Used the amplitude $40$ as the period.
Gave the value of $a$ instead of the period $\dfrac{2\pi}{a}$.

questions.question_text: The depth of water at a wharf is modelled by $d=3\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{6}\right)+10$ metres, where $t$ is the number of hours after $8$ am. Find every value of $t$ in $0\le t\le12$ for which the depth is $11.5$ m.

options.why: Stopped at the first angle and missed the second solution in the domain.
Used $2\pi-\theta$ for the second angle, which is the rule for cosine, not sine.
Used $2\pi-\theta$ for the second angle and lost the first solution.

questions.solution_text:
$3\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{6}\right)+10=11.5$
$3\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{6}\right)=1.5$
$\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{6}\right)=\dfrac{1}{2}$
For $0\le t\le12$ the angle $\dfrac{\pi t}{6}$ runs from $0$ to $2\pi$.
$\dfrac{\pi t}{6}=\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ or $\dfrac{5\pi}{6}$
$t=1$ or $t=5$

questions.question_text: The depth of water in a lock is modelled by $h=4\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{6}\right)+11$ metres, where $t$ is the number of hours after midnight. For how many of the first $12$ hours is the depth at least $13$ m?

options.why: Counted only the interval $0\le t\le2$ and missed the interval at the end of the domain.
Took the interval between the two crossings, which is where the depth is below $13$ m.
Read the second crossing $t=10$ as the total time rather than as a time of day.

questions.solution_text:
$4\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{6}\right)+11=13$
$4\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{6}\right)=2$
$\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{6}\right)=\dfrac{1}{2}$
For $0\le t\le12$ the angle $\dfrac{\pi t}{6}$ runs from $0$ to $2\pi$.
$\dfrac{\pi t}{6}=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ or $\dfrac{5\pi}{3}$
$t=2$ or $t=10$
The depth starts at its maximum, so it is at least $13$ m for $0\le t\le2$ and for $10\le t\le12$.
$2+2=4$

Maximum $2.8$ m, first lowest point at $t=6$ s
options.why: Read the time of the second maximum instead of the first minimum.

options.text: Maximum $2.0$ m, first lowest point at $t=3$ s
options.why: Read the dashed mean line as the maximum instead of the top of the curve.

options.text: Maximum $2.0$ m, first lowest point at $t=6$ s
options.why: Read the mean line as the maximum and the second maximum as the first minimum.

questions.solution_text:
The top of the curve sits at a height of $2.8$ m.
The curve first reaches its lowest point half a period after the start.
The period is $6$ seconds, so the first lowest point is at $t=3$ seconds.

questions.question_text: The population of a possum colony is modelled by $P=90\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{6}\right)+310$, where $t$ is the number of months after the first count. Which statement best describes a limitation of this model?

options.text: It predicts the same numbers every $12$ months forever, so it cannot show a colony that is slowly dying out.
It cannot predict a population in the first month, because the model needs $t\ge1$.
options.why: The model is defined at every value of $t$, including $t$ between $0$ and $1$.

options.text: It predicts a negative population after a few years, because cosine takes negative values.
options.why: The smallest value the model gives is $310-90=220$, which is never negative.

options.text: It cannot be evaluated when $t$ is not a whole number of months.
options.why: Confuses a continuous model with a discrete one; any value of $t$ may be substituted.

questions.solution_text:
The period is $\dfrac{2\pi}{\frac{\pi}{6}}=12$ months, and the amplitude $90$ never changes.
So the model repeats an identical cycle every year for as long as it is used.
A real colony can grow or decline over several years, and this model cannot show that trend.

questions.question_text: The number of visitors to a park each day is modelled by $N=350\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{6}\right)+1200$, where $t$ is the number of months after January. How many visitors does the model predict for $t=5$, to the nearest whole number?

options.why: Took $\cos\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right)$ as positive, so added $303$ instead of subtracting it.
Used $\cos\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right)=-\dfrac{1}{2}$ instead of $-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$.
Used $\cos\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right)=1$, adding the whole amplitude.
